# Power station size for a fridge during an outage

**Short answer:** get a station with at least 1,300 W of surge output and about 1,400 Wh of capacity for one day. Go to about 2,800 Wh for two days. A ~1,000 Wh unit covers roughly 17 hours.

## The three checks

1. **Continuous watts:** A full-size fridge runs at about 100-250 W, so nearly any 1,000 W-class station handles it ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge watts:** The compressor's startup spike is roughly 1,000-2,400 W depending on the fridge. Sources suggest planning for 1,200-1,300 W or more. This is the spec that most often fails, so a big battery with a weak inverter can still trip ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time. A typical efficient fridge averages roughly 41 W, or about 1,000 Wh per day. With inverter losses and 20% headroom, that works out to about 1,400 Wh per day ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). Pick a pure sine wave inverter.

For a more precise number, check your fridge's EnergyGuide label. Divide kWh/year by 8,760 and multiply by 1,000 to get average watts. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can average about twice the typical figure, so go bigger in that case.

## Rough sizing

| Outage | Capacity to look for |
|---|---|
| Up to ~12-17 hours | ~1,000 Wh |
| 24 hours | ~1,400-2,000 Wh |
| 2 days | ~2,800 Wh or an expandable unit |

Keep the door closed. The USDA says food is unsafe after 4 hours above 40°F with the door closed ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).

## Options from the results

- **BLUETTI AC200L** (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, expandable to 8 kWh, LiFePO4): about 33 hours of fridge runtime in HomeGridHQ's estimate. The store price is $899, and the Dealectric page lists a 5% code (AFF5OFF) that brings it to $854.05. [Product page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l) · [Buy at BLUETTI](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l). That buy link is an affiliate link, and the store's checkout has the final word on price.
- **Anker SOLIX S2000** (2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak, pure sine wave): listed at $699.99 after coupon. [Anker SOLIX page](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)
- **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak, $399-699 recently seen), **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** and **EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro** are the ~1,000 Wh picks for shorter outages. They're covered in [BlackBox Supplies' guide](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), but the results didn't include direct purchase links for them.

If you only need to bridge a typical overnight outage, a ~1,000 Wh unit is enough. If you want a full day or more of margin, or want to add a few other loads, a ~2,000 Wh unit like the AC200L or S2000 is the safer choice.

If you tell me your fridge's size and age (or its kWh/year), I can narrow this down.
